objective: Implement a ROS-free deterministic joint-control core over the approved motion ports. It plans bounded quintic position trajectories, creates bounded velocity commands, and summarizes observed tracking samples. It is a planning and measurement primitive only: it does not dispatch, simulate, persist evidence, update WorldState, or claim Gazebo, MuJoCo, hardware, task, or verification success.
acceptance: The ROS-free joint-control core accepts one configured robot identity, exact ordered joints, and explicit per-joint position, velocity, acceleration, and jerk limits. Identity, order, vector length, non-finite values, missing/extra limits, and out-of-bounds feedback or targets fail closed.

Position planning reuses quintic_point_to_point and shares its duration and derivative-limit proof; velocity command construction rejects any value outside the explicit per-joint velocity limit and produces only an internal RobotCommand.

Tracking samples record desired and observed position, velocity, acceleration, and jerk. Deterministic summaries include per-joint position/velocity error, RMS/max errors, peak acceleration/jerk, integrated squared jerk smoothness, and offline settling time using explicit tolerance values.

The implementation is side-effect free and imports no ROS, Gazebo, MuJoCo, MoveIt, hardware adapter, task runtime, public schema, event store, or verifier. It has no transport, simulator, or physical execution claim.
Tests cover a UR5e-shaped named-joint fixture, deterministic planning/metrics, limit rejection, discontinuous sample rejection, no-settling behavior, and zero-duration holds.
commands: docker compose run --rm dashboard python3 tools/scripts/validate_contracts.py

evidence: Task Packet validation output proving the exact changed-path boundary.
Focused red and green uv pytest output for deterministic joint planning and tracking metrics.
Docker contract, scenario, and context validation output.
Git diff limited to the Task Packet, joint-control core, and its tests.
stop_conditions: Implementation requires a public contract/schema, ROS/Gazebo/MuJoCo/MoveIt adapter, launch/configuration, task runtime, event/replay, or hardware change.
The trajectory generator cannot prove position, velocity, acceleration, and jerk limits without changing its existing implementation.
The control core would need to fabricate observed feedback, simulator results, or a verified execution outcome.
Required tests or checks fail for a reason that cannot be fixed inside allowed_paths.
